headlines.label: Vector
headlines.note: k-nearest over a derive: 'vector' column at 50,000 × 768: every path answers the identical top-k before a timing prints. The plan is 15.21× the same query with no column and 6.83× the resident sweep with no database at all; the column costs 2.06× the write. sqlite-vec answers 5.64× faster out of a database 6.59× smaller that holds no documents — see the suite page

headlines.label: Series
headlines.rival: no library rival — the routes a consumer already has
headlines.note: The temporal ground at 100,000 samples, measured before a kernel existed and re-measured against every route since. A sorted cut answers a one-hour range 98.19× a full filter, and a declared epoch column under an index answers it 52.19× the same range read back out of the stored JSON with date functions. A bucket whose floating mean the engine adds over the index-bounded fetch is 1.12× slower than the generic query route; a rolling window is a named refinement instead, costing 18.74× the kernel over an array already in memory. The durable range costs 649.91× the resident cut, which is the price of never having read the rest of the corpus — see the suite page
